newsitem.title: CHINA: Russian PM arrives in China to boost trade ties.
newsitem.headline: Russian PM arrives in China to boost trade ties.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin arrived in Beijing on Thursday on a three-day visit to boost economic ties with a multi-billion dollar natural gas deal in the pipeline.

Chernomyrdin touched down first to tour factories in booming Shenzhen, site of some of China's most ambitious economic reforms, and to meet Guangdong provincial officials before flying to Beijing, a Russian embassy spokesman said.
He flew into Beijing after a day spent touring the high-technology industries of China's showcase of economic reform.
Chernomyrdin is scheduled to meet his Chinese counterpart Li Peng on Friday and the two are expected to sign a multi-billion dollar oil and natural gas pact, diplomats have said.
The two leaders are also expected to sign a rail agreement that aims to improve rail freight between the two neighbours, the diplomats said.

Chernomyrdin's visit has been preceded by a trip by several economic and energy officials, including First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov and Minister of Foreign Trade Mikhail Fradkov, who have been hammering out details of the deals.

Nemtsov was to visit the site of the Three Gorges dam on the Yangtze River on Thursday after Premier Li suddenly invited him to tour the giant hydroelectric and water conservancy project, a Russian embassy spokesman said earlier but gave no details.
A Russian consortium is bidding for a big contract to supply 14 generators with a total installed capacity of 9,800 megawatts for the hydroelectric power station.

The China Yangtze Three Gorges Development Corp has said it was still reviewing tenders from several consortia to supply the generating units and had planned to select the winning bidder by late June or early July.
Officials have said a decision has yet to be announced.

Diplomats said Chernomyrdin's visit was aimed chiefly at boosting lagging economic ties with China after a series of high-level official exchanges and presidential summits have bolstered political relations between Moscow and Beijing.
